text:
Maria Chen: quick architecture q: we need a minimal runtime DSL for quant profiles so the scheduler + router can reason about safety and cost. thoughts on shape?
Ajay Patel: keep it tiny. fields: name, bitwidth, quality_tier, fallback_policy, max_latency_pct, cost_multiplier. example: 
```
name: fp8_risky
bitwidth: fp8
quality_tier: medium
fallback_policy: fallback_to_int8
max_latency_pct: 120
cost_multiplier: 0.85
```
Devin Torres: add an explicit compatibility list for kernels/hardware (e.g. a100, h100, cpu). prevents runtime surprises.
Sophie Li: we also need per-endpoint overrides in the policy. product wants strict quality for "search" endpoints but will accept aggressive cost for batch embeddings.
Ravi Kumar: +1 on overrides. propose precedence: endpoint_override > customer_override > global_profile. that way enterprise SLAs can pin quality.
Lena Park: ops note: we'll need rollout hooks: a canary predicate, gradual ramp steps, and auto-rollback on quality regressions. recommend: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with metrics check at each stage.
perf-bot: suggestion: gate on 95th latency and tok-level perplexity. fail if latency increases >10% or perf delta p<0.01.
Ajay Patel: important: define what "quality" means per workload. for convs use conv-turn-level F1 + human escore; for QA use EM+F1; for summarization ROUGE-L. normalize scores into the same degradation scale.
Devin Torres: operational detail: the runtime will tag spans with `quant_profile` and `profile_revision`. required for postmortem.
Sophie Li: human spot check: 100 samples from each canary bucket at every step. we'll crowdsource annotations and keep a simple checklist: hallucination, omission, style-change.
Maria Chen: rollback triggers? auto-rollback if any of these: (1) p-value < 0.01 and delta worse than threshold, (2) customer complaint spike > 2x baseline, (3) manual abort from oncall.
Lena Park: add safety net: if canary hits latency regression but quality is fine, we can pause ramp and change scheduling (reduce batch size) instead of full rollback.
Ravi Kumar: about profiling: we need per-slice metrics for short prompts vs longctx. quant sensitivity is very non-uniform across sequence length.
Ajay Patel: config DSL should be json/yaml friendly and validateable. add schema versioning so old profiles don't break runtime.
Devin Torres: testing: unit tests for profile parsing + e2e smoke that runs a micro-benchmark on each cluster type. CI should block profile merges w/o a successful smoke run.
perf-bot: created perf job template: quant-smoke-{profile}-{hw}. schedule on every PR.
Maria Chen: action items: Ajay draft DSL schema, Devin wire smoke job + tags, Lena draft rollout playbook, Sophie assemble human checklist, Ravi build longctx slices. I'll collate into an RFC next week.
Sophie Li: happy to own checklist. can we agree on a max acceptable 4-bit delta of EM -2.5 pts for non-core endpoints?
Ajay Patel: +1 as default but allow overrides. document everything in RFC.
deploy-bot: note: please include `experimental/quant` label to opt-out gating for research branches.
Maria Chen: thanks all. keeping this thread as single source for the DSL + rollback playbook. ping me if you need a slot on next sync. :thumbsup:
